gen-megrim-gf-geom: Megrim's hairline, angular strokes look cut from glass. Geom answers in a plain sans with a lofty lowercase band, friendly and sturdy where the heading is sharp and futuristic.
gen-megrim-gf-hammersmith-one: Futuristic edges give Megrim a cool, sharp-cornered look up top. And Hammersmith One keeps the text calm in sans form, its rounded cord-like strokes and low capitals making long reading feel smooth.
gen-megrim-gf-inder: Angular and futuristic, Megrim stitches its lines like thread along a path. Inder follows in a clean sans with little difference between capitals and lowercase, so a longer read stays level and uncluttered.
gen-megrim-gf-jaldi: Megrim's c opens as wide as a bent paperclip. Jaldi, a sans with a tall x-height and brushed, tightly packed letters, gives that spare angular heading a sturdier, more approachable footing underneath.
gen-megrim-gf-kdam-thmor-pro: Kdam Thmor Pro fills the line with big bowls, giving the text a modern, contemporary heft. And Megrim's untilted, uniform lines above it keep that weight feeling crisp rather than heavy over a long page.
gen-megrim-gf-krona-one: Megrim looks laser-cut, every line sliced at one width. Krona One brings loosely spaced, cast-iron-tall lowercase in a sans-serif, and the weighty body against that thin, sharp heading is what makes the pair.
gen-megrim-gf-magra: Professional in tone, Megrim draws plain constant-width lines that look sharp and futuristic. Magra, a sans, is the one built to carry words, its big-bodied lowercase doing the steady work the heading leaves alone.
gen-megrim-gf-major-mono-display: Neon glass meets angular wire. Megrim is best at sharp, skyward display lines, while Major Mono Display, a monospace, does its best work with tube-like strokes and wide sidebearings that feel precise and technical.
gen-megrim-gf-martian-mono: Code-terminal looseness sits under a heading of sharp, futuristic edges, each letter of the monospace body spaced far apart. Megrim leads with angles; Martian Mono keeps things structured.
gen-megrim-gf-matemasie: Megrim opens its letters wide, angular and futuristic, with a skyward x-height line. Matemasie then closes its rounds into a clean sans-serif, with broad gaps between glyphs and small entry points, so the heading's openness stands out.
